title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training for Contracting Personnel
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Artificial Intelligence (AI) Training for Contracting Personnel The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District is seeking sources capable of providing comprehensive Artificial Intelligence (AI) training for its contracting and acquisition workforce. The training will be delivered virtually and is intended to establish a common baseline of advanced AI proficiency across the team. This sources-sought announcement is a market research tool to identify businesses with the capability to accomplish the work described herein. This is not a solicitation. No proposals or quotes are requested at this time. Further information regarding this requirement will be available through SAM.gov upon release of any subsequent solicitation. NAICS Code: 611430 � Professional and Management Development Training. The associated small business size standard is $15,000,000. REQUIRED RESPONSE INFORMATION All interested offerors are required to provide the following: A list of current or past projects (within the last five years) demonstrating technical experience with work of a similar nature to that listed in the Summary Scope of Work. For each project submitted, provide a brief narrative statement of the work involved, your firm�s role, the number of participants trained, delivery method (virtual/in-person), the dollar value, and the completion date. Include any special qualifications, certifications, or relevant experience with federal acquisition/contracting training or AI applications in a government context. A reference list for each of the projects submitted in item 1 above. Include the name, title, phone number, and email address for each reference. A statement of your firm�s business size (Small Business, HUBZone Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, or Other-Than-Small Business) with regard to the NAICS code listed above. A statement that your firm intends to submit an offer on the project when it is advertised. Your firm�s CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Confirmation that your firm can comply with FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting), if applicable, by performing at least 50 percent of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel with its own employees or similarly situated entities. Answers to the following capability questions: Experience with Federal Acquisition/Contracting AI Training: Describe your firm�s experience developing and delivering AI-related training specifically tailored to federal acquisition, contracting, or procurement professionals (GS-1102 series or equivalent). Include examples of topics such as AI for market research, Performance Work Statement (PWS) development, prompt engineering for acquisition documents, AI agents for workflow automation, or compliance/governance of AI in acquisition. Ability to Meet Required Learning Outcomes: The Government requires approximately 20 hours of interactive virtual instruction (structured as five roughly 4-hour modules or an equivalent modular structure) that produces the following learning outcomes for a contracting/acquisition workforce. Please describe how your firm�s existing or customizable curriculum maps to each outcome, or how you would structure training to achieve them: Foundational AI and data literacy appropriate for federal employees, including responsible use, bias awareness, security considerations, and compliance frameworks. Practical prompt-engineering skills that enable participants to generate high-quality, usable outputs for acquisition-related work products. Application of AI tools and techniques specifically within the federal acquisition lifecycle (market research, requirements development, documentation, analysis, and related processes) while maintaining FAR and agency compliance. Identification and practical use of AI agents or automation approaches to streamline routine contracting and acquisition workflows. Advanced prompt-design and reasoning strategies that enable participants to evaluate AI-generated content for accuracy, sufficiency, and regulatory compliance in a contracting context. Virtual Delivery & Interactivity: Describe your capabilities for delivering high-quality, interactive virtual instructor-led training (VILT) for groups of up to 30 participants. What platforms do you use? How do you ensure engagement, practical exercises, and hands-on application during virtual sessions? Tailoring Capability: With adequate notice (ideally 4�6 weeks), can you tailor course exercises and examples to the USACE contracting environment (e.g., drafting/editing PWSs, market research reports, acquisition strategies, or notional purchasing data)? Describe your process for incorporating customer-provided or jointly developed relevant examples. Instructor Qualifications: What are the typical qualifications and experience of instructors who would deliver AI training focused on federal acquisition? Do instructors have practical experience in contracting/acquisition, AI/ML applications in government, or both? Certificates & CLPs: Do you issue completion certificates? Can training be structured to support Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) for the Defense Acquisition Workforce (approximately 20 CLPs total for a 20-hour curriculum)? Pricing Structure: What pricing structures are most standard for group virtual training of this nature (e.g., firm-fixed-price per course/module for up to 30 participants, per-student pricing, or package pricing for a multi-module curriculum)? Provide rough order of magnitude (ROM) pricing if available for planning purposes. Capacity & Schedule: Can your firm support delivery of approximately 20 hours of virtual instruction during the February�March 2027 timeframe (or similar Q2 FY27 window), with scheduling flexibility for the Government? What is your typical lead time for group enrollments and any minor course tailoring? Session Recording for Internal Repository: Does your firm permit the Government to record the virtual training sessions for internal repository and reference purposes (e.g., for personnel who miss a session or for future onboarding)? If recording is permitted, what conditions or restrictions apply (platform limitations, instructor intellectual property, participant consent, time-limited access, etc.)? Please indicate whether allowing recording would impact price and, if so, the approximate magnitude of that impact. Larger-Scale Sessions for Technical Customers / Requirements Writers: In addition to the core contracting-workforce curriculum (approximately 30 participants), the District is interested in market feedback on the feasibility of larger virtual sessions (potentially 100+ participants) aimed at technical customers, project managers, and requirements writers. These sessions would focus on responsible AI use in the development of requirements documents and technical evaluations. Real-world problem areas include: (1) technical customers using AI to draft scopes of work or specifications that inadvertently lock to a single manufacturer�s product because prompts fail to solicit competition-friendly language allowing multiple technically acceptable solutions; and (2) technical customers using AI for analysis of proposals/quotes but applying incomplete or biased prompts that result in incorrect rejection of otherwise acceptable offers or acceptance of offers that do not meet the stated requirements. Please address: (a) whether your firm currently offers, or could rapidly develop, content tailored to these use cases; (b) recommended format and length for such sessions; (c) pricing implications or structure for cohorts of 100+ versus the smaller group model; and (d) any best practices or cautionary notes for delivering effective large-scale virtual AI training to mixed technical audiences. title: Pine Bluff Arsenal Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: The services provided include surface water, sediment, and fish tissue sampling in streams and large river systems, as well as ambient sediment toxicity testing to determine the effectiveness of corrective measures. Acute and chronic whole effluent toxicity testing is conducted for four NPDES permitted outfalls, with the capability to perform Toxicity Identification Evaluation and Toxicity Reduction Evaluation if needed. Additionally, statistical analysis is compiled and conducted for three RCRA Detection monitoring groundwater assessment reports (covering three regulated units) and twelve RCRA Corrective Action Closure sites annually. Maintenance and updating of the PBA-specific Geographic Information System database is also included. The services encompass preparing industrial stormwater permit renewals, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and stormwater sampling for three outfalls, as well as preparation of Construction SWPPPs and permits. Compliance assistance is provided for SPCC Plan development and review, RCRA Permit development and review, and CAA permit review, renewal, and reporting. The services also support a change of the State of Arkansas Water Quality Standards, Rule 2, for mercury at an NPDES outfall, and assist with contaminant transport investigations in Phillips Creek and the Arkansas River. *Amendment 0001 posted 12 November 2026

description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to award an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Quality Assurance Services across Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. This procurement follows the presolicitation notice previously synopsized under solicitation number W51DQV26RA007. The contractor shall provide comprehensive quality assurance oversight supporting Civil Works, International and Interagency Services (IIS), and Military Construction (MILCON) projects, including navigation, flood risk management, coastal protection, environmental restoration, water resources, and military or federal installations. Services encompass monitoring contractor compliance with plans and specifications, reviewing engineering submittals and technical reports, conducting on-site field inspections of dams, levees, berms, cutoff walls, pump stations, flood control gates, and electrical systems, and performing certified sampling and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, and water. Contract personnel shall also perform daily safety monitoring and prepare daily quality assurance inspection reports. This action is a total small business set-aside under NAICS code 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) with an applicable small business size standard of $19.5 million. The contract ordering period comprises a one-year base period, four 12-month option periods, and one six-month option period, not to exceed a total duration of five years and six months, with a maximum program capacity of $35 million across the contract life.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAT27Q0003 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Airport BAER Seed Collection within the Trabuco Ranger District of the Cleveland National Forest. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 115310, Support Activities for Forestry The small business size standard is $11.5M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov prior to submission of quotations to be eligible for award. Lack of SAM registration will make a contractor ineligible for award. Period of Performance for this requirement is date of award through 30 September 2027. The intent of this project is to procure services to locate, identify and map collection sites of native plant species; to collect seed from these native species; to clean, store, and deliver the collected seed to the Cleveland National Forest to support post-fire restoration projects within the Airport Fire burn area. The contractor will work and communicate with Forest staff to determine and identify collection species and sites. Up to approximately 100-300 lbs of native plant seed shall be collected during this project. description: Request for Information (RFI) Department of the Navy (DON). Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY (as defined in FAR 15.101(c)); this is not a solicitation. A formal solicitation is not available at this time. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government and does not obligate the Government to award a contract or pay for the information provided in response. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. In accordance with FAR 15.101 (c), RFI, the Government does not currently intend to award a contract, but wants to obtain price, delivery, market, or capabilities information for planning purposes. Responses to RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. Information received in response to this RFI will be safeguarded adequately from unauthorized disclosure. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THIS RFI Response Format/Page Limitations: As this is not a proposal the Government recommends a clear concise response and requests responses be limited to 25 pages or less. Interested parties should limit marketing material to allow for direct and substantive responses to the information requested by the Government. IMPORTANT NOTE: If your company has an existing contracting vehicle that can fulfill this need (e.g., GSA Schedule, NAVFAC MAC/MACC, or any other existing contract/Basic Ordering Agreement), please provide enough information in your response for the Government to analyze those resources to include points of contact, contract number/name, etc. Any responding contractor may respond to any number of questions posed in this RFI (items A-H below); a submission does not mandate a response to each question asked. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond. High-Level Scope of Work Hangar Procurement & Erection: Turnkey procurement, delivery, and complete erection of two (2) temporary, Relocatable Metal Building (RMB) hangars (approximately 40,000 SF clear interior space each), including hangar doors, exhaust ventilation systems, provisions for overhead crane support, fire protection/suppression, lightning protection, physical security, and relocatable administrative/support modular units. Civil & Structural Construction: Mass grading, site excavation, drainage, backfill, and construction of reinforced concrete foundation slabs (approximately 40,000 SF each) with associated strip/spread footings, perimeter walls, and specialized protective floor coatings/sealers. Airfield Pavements: Construction of heavy-duty aircraft access aprons, taxiways, towaways, tug pads, and administrative vehicle hardstands connecting to existing airfield networks. Approximate size of 62,000 SF. Utility Infrastructure & Site Improvements: Extension, connection, and rerouting of comprehensive site utilities (domestic water, sanitary sewer piping and manholes, storm drainage, natural gas, underground electrical conductors, duct banks, manholes, and oil/water separation) and airfield security fence relocation with a new Access Control Point (ACP). The purpose of this RFI is to gather market intelligence on acquisition vehicles, current construction costs, RMB manufacturing and delivery lead times, project phasing, and industry best practices for airfield construction projects. A. Company Information Required All responding sources must submit a response in accordance with the information provided below. Company Name and Address Point of Contact (Name, Phone Number, Email) Company Business Size and Status (e.g., Large, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB) Primary NAICS code(s) (e.g. 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction) SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC) available for this work B. Corporate Capabilities & Experience Vendors should address their specific capabilities in executing federal construction projects, specifically near an active airfield. Similar Experience: Provide two (2) to three (3) examples of similar commercial or federal RMB construction projects completed within the last seven (7) years. Highlight any work performed within close proximity of active airports/airfields. Federal Access: Confirm your firm�s capability to adhere to military installation security requirements and obtain DBIDS (Defense Biometric Identification System) credentials for personnel access at Naval Air Station (NAS) Jacksonville, FL. C. Cost Estimation & Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) The Government seeks Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimates strictly for budgetary planning and market research. Pricing submitted is non-binding. Based on standard industry practices for a facility of this type, please provide a ROM breakdown and address the following cost elements: Cost Element Provide cost breakdown in the following manner: Phased ROM Estimate 1. Phase 1 Base Bid: Hangar 1 and foundation, 41,540 SF airfield pavement and site improvements including utilities for a complete and usable facility. Phase 1 must be complete by DEC2028. 2. Phase 2 Option 1: Hangar 2 and foundation, 20,460 SF airfield pavement and site improvements including utilities for a complete and usable facility. Phase 2 must be completed by DEC2029. If Option 1 is awarded with Base Bid or before Base Bid completion construction for both phases can be parallel. D. Cost Drivers What do you anticipate being the most significant cost drivers for a temporary hangar project specifically located at NAS Jacksonville Florida? E. Market Volatility Are there current supply chain constraints, equipment shortages, or labor rate spikes in the Northeast Florida market that the Government should account for in its budgetary estimates? F. Value Engineering What commercial best practices or alternative methods could the Government incorporate into the final Statement of Work to safely lower the overall project cost and reduce construction duration? G. Schedule: How many calendar days would you estimate for a standard RMB project of this nature, factoring in standard Northeast Florida weather delays? H. Industry Feedback: Government-Provided Information To maximize competition and ensure accurate pricing in a future formal solicitation, the Government seeks to understand what specific data the industry requires. What specific documents, site data, or surveys does your firm need from the Government in a formal solicitation package to provide a highly accurate, firm-fixed-price proposal? (e.g., specific types of hazardous material surveys, utility disconnect maps, laydown area dimensions, historical as-built drawings, etc.) Point of Contact & Submission Responses are due no later than 2:00 PM Eastern Time, November 20, 2026, via email to Lindsay Betteridge at lindsay.e.betteridge.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil Please note "RFI Response: Temp Hangar NAS JAX; N6945027RTEMP" in the subject line of your response. Mark your response as "Proprietary Information" if the information is considered business sensitive. The email file size shall not exceed 10 MB.

title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. title: TR-143A TRANSDUCERS
description: ITEM DESCRIPTION - Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane (NSWC Crane) has a requirement to procure TR-143A Transducers, Part Number: 7146100-302. These transducers are utilized in the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem, supporting United States (U.S) Navy and United Kingdom (UK) Ballistic Missile Submarine Nuclear Powered submarines as part of the Navigation Subsystem Sonar. These transducers are used in coordination with TR-333 Hydrophones to receive signals from the ocean floor and to improve submarine launch accuracy. The transducers are manufactured items used as replacement assets during normal refit, replenish, and replacement operations for the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem and support U.S. Ohio and Columbia class submarines in addition to UK Vanguard and Dreadnought class submarines. The proposed contract action is for a two-year ordering period extension and ceiling increase, on contract N0016426DGP87, a firm-fixed-price, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity contract with a five-year ordering period. The contract is for supplies which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Massa Products Corporation, Hingham, MA 02043 (CAGE 88958), under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (c) (2), only one responsible source. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis, because the supplies have been deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued production of highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source would result in (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Additionally, the Government is pursuing a sole source procurement to mitigate associated certification costs and certification testing that can take up to thirty-six months to complete. Furthermore, if a potential vendor is not capable of meeting the certification requirements, there is high likelihood that ship schedules will be significantly impacted. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract extension based upon responses to the solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of re-evaluating the justification for sole source or limitation of sources and making a determination to change the acquisition strategy to a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Questions or inquiries should be directed to Steven Junkins, Code 0232, e-mail steven.l.junkins2.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the above solicitation number when responding to this notice.

description: Pre-Solicitation Notice/Synopsis - Naval Air Station (NAS) Corpus Christi, Texas, SPE603-27-R-5X03 Government Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft and Ground Fuel Services, Bulk Fuel Storage and Distribution Services at NAS Corpus Christi, TX. This is a Pre-solicitation Notice to Sources Sought Notice posted under SPE603-26-R-5X20. This Pre-solicitation notice SPE603-27-R-5X03 is for GOCO services at NAS Corpus Christi, TX. Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy-FESAB will be issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for fuel services to include all personnel, equipment, vehicles, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform aircraft and ground fuel support services at NAS Corpus Christi, TX. The contractor shall be responsible for a comprehensive range of fuel-related services. This includes the management, operation, maintenance, product quality surveillance, inventory and accounting controls, security, safety, and environmental protection of the assets, properties, and performance duties as identified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The contractor�s duties shall encompass the following: Fuel Operations: Receiving, storing, testing, and issuing aviation and ground fuels. Bulk Fuel Storage: Managing two 6,000-barrel aboveground fuel storage tanks and associated infrastructure. Fuel Servicing: Providing mobile refueling and defueling services for aircraft, including support for outlying fields (NOLF Cabaniss, NOLF Waldron, and NOLF Goliad on an emergency basis). Ground Fuel Services: Operating and maintaining the base service station, which dispenses unleaded and diesel fuel. Quality Surveillance: Ensuring fuel products meet all required specifications through sampling, testing, and laboratory operations. Maintenance: Performing operator-level maintenance on all government-furnished equipment and facilities. Safety and Environmental Compliance: Adhering to all applicable Department of Defense (DoD), federal, state, and local regulations. The contractor will be required to: Provide all necessary personnel, equipment, and supplies to perform the services outlined in the PWS. Develop and submit detailed plans for contract compliance, quality control, maintenance, staffing, and safety. Utilize a contractor-furnished Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to track and report on all maintenance activities. Meet all performance requirements and be subject to quality assurance monitoring by the government. Ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. Provide 24/7 fuel dispatch services and be prepared to support unscheduled and emergency fueling requirements. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage), and the size standard is $36.5 million. title: U.S. Army Contracting Command � Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) Army Manufacturing Rodeo: sUAS Manufacturing Rodeo
description: Background for Army Manufacturing Rodeo: Contemporary peer and near-peer conflicts have fundamentally reshaped modern multi-dominant warfare. Small Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (sUAS), autonomous systems, and loitering strike munitions are being consumed at consumption rates and volume comparable to conventional tube artillery. Prevailing operational environments necessitate deep operational magazines, high-velocity resupply cycles, and continuous tactical adaptation at the tactical edge. However, traditional defense acquisition and defense industrial manufacturing architecture remain optimized for boutique, low-rate production of highly specialized, high-cost platforms. These legacy paradigms are characterized by: Rigid, proprietary tooling with limited multi-vendor cross-compatibility; Fragile, multi-tiered subcomponent supply chains with hidden foreign adversary dependencies; Single-point supplier vulnerabilities and prohibitive unit procurement costs; and Inflexible production lines incapable of dynamically scaling to wartime surge capacity during national mobilization. To achieve strategic overmatch in prolonged combat operations, the Department of the Army requires a paradigm shift toward "Affordable Mass"�the deliberate capability to procure, field, and sustain expendable, lethal autonomous munitions at an industrial scale and velocity that overwhelms adversary defenses and replenishes combat losses faster than attrition occurs. In response to rapid developments in uncrewed aerial combat, the Army launched foundational initiatives including Project Jailbreak and the Drone Dominance Program (DDP) to rapidly evaluate, iterate, and integrate commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) and modified commercial drone technology into tactical formations. While these early initiatives demonstrated the decisive tactical utility of commercial FPV (First-Person View) systems and accelerated soldier touchpoints, they simultaneously illuminated critical industrial vulnerabilities: commercial vendors often struggle with raw manufacturing surge capacity, supply chain assurance, and compliance with rigorous military safety and lethality standards. To bridge this divide, the Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Acquisition, Logistics, and Technology (ASA(ALT)), in close coordination with Army Materiel Command (AMC) and Army Contracting Command � Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA), is launching the sUAS portion of Supply-Chain stress testing as the operational baseline for the Army�s inaugural Manufacturing Rodeo. Rather than subsidizing the buildout of bespoke, isolated commercial factories that remain vulnerable to peacetime contraction and component scarcity, the goal is to operationalize a novel, cooperative hybrid manufacturing framework. This model pairs the massive capital infrastructure, machining capacity, and energetic handling capabilities of the Army�s Organic Industrial Base (OIB) with the design agility, software innovation, and rapid iteration speed of the commercial Defense Industrial Base (DIB). sUAS Manufacturing This Area of Interest solicits commercial solutions specifically focused on standardizing and mass-producing an attainable Group 1 FPV One-Way Attack (OWA) and Loitering Strike commodity line. Unit Cost Restriction: The cost of the Group 1 FPV One-Way Attack (OWA) platform is strictly restricted to a maximum of $3,000 per unit. To validate compliance with this unit cost cap and ensure supply chain integrity, submitters must include a complete Bill of Materials (BOM) using Attachment C (DCMA BOM Template) detailing all subcomponents, wafer fabrication, and manufacturing origins. Participating systems must meet rigorous operational and interoperability thresholds, including: Terminal Standoff & Precision Strike: Capability to locate, track, and kinetically engage moving and stationary target sets (personnel in defilade, armored fighting vehicles, command posts) across tactical distances ranging from close-combat environments out to extended standoff depths. Electromagnetic Warfare & GNSS-Denied Resilience: Proven flight capability in severe electronic warfare (EW) environments, incorporating frequency-agile, multi-band command and control (C2) links, zero-RF-signature fiber-optic tethered options, and alternate navigation modalities such as visual odometry. Control Ratio Architecture (1:20): Operational architecture capable of supporting a 1:20 ratio�where twenty (20) expendable air vehicles are controlled, bound, and selectively launched via a single durable Ground Control Station (GCS) with minimal operator overhead. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: TACDS Services
description: Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport, has a requirement for fleet installation and sparing for TACDS units. These TACDS units require battery replacement every five years, otherwise they will not be suitable for fleet use. The anticipated dollar amount is $44,800 for sixteen (16) TACDS units to be screened, have their batteries swapped, reset to factory settings, and corrected firmware updated. This effort will providea assets available to support anticipated demand. These TACDS units are supported on a Sole Source basis because only General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has the capability to replace existing batteries, complete the factory reset, and establish correct firmware. The TACDS units created by GDMS have been shock tested in the cabinets and is therefore the only unit approved for use in the existing platform. The design, development and environmental qualification efforts associated with an alternate would be cost prohibitive for the overall program. Furthermore, the requalification process would be detrimental to the overall program. Based on the above, it is not reasonable to conclude the potential savings from competition can offset the duplicative cost and schedule/mission impact associated with purchasing a new brand name product. Therefore, it is in the best interest of the government to solicit this requirement on brand name only basis. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals; however, any interested party that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation. The Government will consider all responses received within the posting period as market research. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. title: Design-Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood, TX
description: *****AMENDMENT 0003 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON MONDAY, 02 NOVEMBER 2026**** *****AMENDMENT 0002 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON MONDAY, 19 OCTOBER 2026**** *****AMENDMENT 0001 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026***** Request for Proposal (RFP), Solicitation No. W912QR25RA013 is issued for the repair of a failing Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood (formerly Fort Cavazos), TX. This project will repair and construct an addition to an existing ~26,000 square feet of the maintenance part of the Equipment Concentration Site, Maintenance Building 56767, that is in a failing condition, and has not undergone any major infrastructure or system repairs, only limited maintenance and repair work has occurred. The project includes repair of HVAC and Electrical systems, remove non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspace, restore inadequate and non-code compliant bathrooms, repair light fixtures with code compliant units, failed flooring, code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, repair electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided to include a code compliant entrance ramp. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. This project contains options. The contract duration is estimated at 913 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP).This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF). TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: Total Small Business Set-Aside Procurement. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design/Build procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection process. The technical information contained in each Offeror s proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Phase II Selected Offerors are requested to submit additional information described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, Schedule Narrative, and Price. The Standard Form (SF) 1442, resubmission of Evidence of Ability to Obtain Bonding and Proof of Financial Ability, and resubmission of Pre-Award Information will also be required. All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. NEGOTIATIONS: The Government intends to award without negotiations, but reserves the right to conduct negotiations should it be deemed in the Government s best interest. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The estimated construction magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS: Paper copies of the solicitation and amendments will not be issued. Telephone, email, and fax requests for this solicitation, amendments, and attachments (plans and specifications) will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To be able to download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the System for Award Management at https ://sam.gov. Amendments, when issued, will be posted to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Portal and SAM.gov websites for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the websites periodically for any and all amendments to the solicitation. System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror .POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Bonny Dylewski, at bonny.c.dylewski@usace.army.mil. description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: Secured Janitorial Services. Marine Corps Base, Quantico, VA 22134-2134 SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR SECURED JANITORIAL SERVICES AT MARINE CORPS BASE (MCB) QUANTICO, VA. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington/Facilities, Engineering, and Acquisition Division (FEAD) Quantico is seeking Small Business Administration�s eligible certified 8(a) participants capable of performing secured janitorial services for Marine Corps Base Quantico, (MCBQ). THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL USED TO DETERMINE THE AVAILABILITY AND ADEQUACY OF POTENTIAL CERTIFIED 8(A) SOURCES PRIOR TO DETERMINING THE METHOD OF ACQUISITION AND ISSUANCE OF AN AWARD. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. Respondents will not be notified of the evaluation. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. No telephone calls or emails will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement, if any, that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The appropriate NAICS Code is 561720, Janitorial Services, and the corresponding size Standard is $22.0 million. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by FEAD Quantico, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The intent of this notice is to identify potential Offerors for market research purposes. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to identify eligible certified 8(a) participants with the primary NAICS 561720, capacity, experience, and interest in the secured janitorial services for three secured buildings within the area of responsibility of Marine Corps Base Quantico, (MCBQ) VA. The secured janitorial recurring work is summarily described as: Provide all labor, supervision, management, coordination, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide janitorial services in various secured buildings at MCB Quantico. This requirement includes non-recurring work (also known as Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)) wherein task orders for pre-priced contract line items or negotiated labor and materials for services in excess of recurring services are issued. Interested sources shall demonstrate the experience and capability in the services described above, demonstrate the ability to transition to 100% operational capacity within 60 days or less, and the capability to provide secure janitorial staff. All work under the contract is performed in secure areas and all Contractor personnel requiring access to a secure area shall possess an active final Top Secret Facility Clearance (access to COMSEC and NATO) without any Special Limitations that restrict access. Interim clearances are not accepted for TS/SCI contract efforts. The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring all contract personnel are U.S. citizens and possess an in-scope (per current DoD 6-year reinvestigation requirement), favorable, Single Scope Background Investigation (SSBI) / T5 investigation (to include SBPR, PPR or T5R), or currently enrolled in the DoD Continuous Evaluation (CE) / Continuous Vetting (CV) program, adjudicated for Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) eligibility by the DoD Central Adjudication Facility (DoD CAF) without conditions, exceptions, or waivers at the time of award and prior to performance under this contract. The Contractor shall ensure it and any subcontractors have completed all DD Form 254 requirements prior to commencing any work under this contract. The request shall be renewed annually or for the duration of the contract if less than one year. If awarded, the contract will consist of a base period and four (4) one-year option periods. If, at the end of the contract term, the Government does not award a follow-on contract in time, the Government may require the Contractor to continue performance for an additional period of up to six months under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Clause 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services. In accordance with FAR Part 15, this project will be procured utilizing contracting by negotiations. All certified, eligible 8(a) participants capable of performing this work are encouraged to respond. Capabilities Statement Packets: It is requested that all responsible, interested certified 8(a) participants submit a capabilities statement package demonstrating ability to perform the requested services. The document must be no more than 3 pages in length, singled-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman font minimum, excluding title page. This documentation shall address, at a minimum, the following: (1) Company profile to include number of employees, office location(s), Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Cage Code, VETS 4212 Proof of Submission and a statement regarding small business designation and status and any certifications to the designation. (2) Relevant Experience of three (3) recent and completed projects. Details should include whether the concern was a prime or subcontractor, contract value, square footage and a brief description of the scope performed, contracting agency, contract number, title, place of performance, years of performance, value of contract per year, and any security requirements. The Government reserves the right to request additional information as needed from all respondents. The Statement of Capabilities package must be complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the NAVFAC team to determine the firm�s capabilities. Information submitted will only be considered for this sources sought. Responses, questions, or comments shall be emailed to Ms. Luz M. Baron, Contract Specialist Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: luz.m.baron.civ@us.navy.mil or Ms. Dotty M. Medel, Contract Specialist Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: dotty.m.medel.civ@us.navy.mil All responses must be received no later than November 20, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST. Submissions received after this deadline will not be evaluated. Only email responses will be entertained. Thank you for your interest and support of NAVFAC Washington and the Warfighter.

description: ITEM DESCRIPTION - The items to be procured are Hydrophone Transformers are used in the manufacture of US and UK TR-333 Hydrophones for the Navigation Subsystem produced by NSWC Crane, currently deployed in the Submarine Fleet. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis, because the supplies have been deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued production of highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source would result in (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Additionally, the Government is pursuing a sole source procurement to mitigate associated certification costs and delays required for certification testing. Furthermore, if a potential vendor is not capable of meeting the certification requirements, there is high likelihood that mission schedules will be significantly impacted. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Aviation, Richmond proposes to issue a Letter Request for Proposal (RFP) to support a DLA Strategic Initiative. A total of 153 NSNs for various platforms / weapon systems are targeted for this RFP and contract action. OEM Parker Hannifin Corporation (59211) has been identified as the approved source of supply for the listed items; therefore, the proposed action is intended to be awarded on a sole source basis to the OEM. It is anticipated that 153 items will be awarded and priced with lead-times as add-ons to the OEM's existing Long-Term Contracts (LTCs): Captains of Industry (COI) Supplier Capabilities Contract (SCC) SPE4AX-21-D-9402 for commercial items and SPE4AX-21-D-9403 for military unique items. These items have been identified as sole source; however, some items may have history showing awards to other than the OEM. Surplus dealers are also invited to respond to this synopsis. title: Construct Interim Remedial Action (IRA) for the Nelson Tunnel Superfund Site
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is not a solicitation and any offers received as a result of this pre-solicitation notice will not be accepted or evaluated. USACE Omaha District intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) solicitation W9128F27RA056 for the following action in November 2026 with the planned proposal due date in January 2027. ***PLEASE REFERENCE THE SITE VISIT INSTRUCTIONS IN THE ATTACHED DOCUMENT AND RESPOND NO LATER THAN THE DATE SHOWN. Project Title: Construct Interim Remedial Action (IRA) for the Nelson Tunnel Superfund Site Project Location: One mile north of the town of Creede in Mineral County, Colorado NAICS Code: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction PSC Code: Y1LC - Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures Set-Asides: This solicitation will be issued unrestricted; both small and large businesses are encouraged to participate. Synopsis of Project: Construction Services for the Nelson Tunnel/Commodore Waste Rock Site (Nelson Tunnel Site or Site), the focus of the interim remedial action (IRA), consists of an abandoned underground hard rock mine and drainage tunnel with several shafts, crosscuts and drafts branching off the main tunnel. The remedial action objective of the RA is to reduce the likelihood of a large, uncontrolled release of mine-impacted water from mine pools impounded within the Nelson Tunnel. The selected alternative for the Nelson Tunnel Interim Record of Decision (IROD) is to construct a bypass adit that connects into Nelson Tunnel at a sufficient distance from the surface to allow for installation of a flow-through hydraulic bulkhead within Nelson Tunnel. The IROD selected remedy is Alternative 4, Drive New Adit to Intersect Nelson Tunnel, Tunnel Rehabilitation, Install Bulkhead in Nelson Tunnel and Flow Control Structure in Commodore 5 level and include the following remedial components. 1. Installation of a new adit south of Nelson Tunnel, to bypass the Nelson Tunnel Portal Pool. 2. Rehabilitation of Nelson Tunnel from the bypass adit connection to the location where bulkhead construction is planned. 3. Installation of a flow control bulkhead in Nelson Tunnel to protect against a sudden uncontrolled release through Nelson Tunnel.4. Installation of an accessible bulkhead flow control structure in the Commodore 5 level to protect against a sudden uncontrolled release through this level. Additional Information can be found at the following EPA website provided in the attachment.

title: Laboratory Capabilities to Test Railroad Tank Car Thermal Protection Systems (TPS)
description: Request for Information (RFI) only. Purpose This RFI seeks information regarding Laboratory Capabilities to perform pool and torch fire tests of Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) to the U.S. DOT Volpe Center. A qualified vendor must be capable of performing pool and torch fire tests as described in 49 CFR 179 Appendix B. The vendor should also be capable of performing light fabrication and/or assembly of test specimens for the aforementioned tests. Qualified vendors are requested to respond as detailed further below, which includes capability, small business classification, estimated lead time including any risks that may impact delivery, and any other industry concerns the government might consider before solicitation. The intent is to gather information to inform a possible future procurement or contract. Background The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) is conducting research into the performance of TPS for railroad tank cars. TPS are designed to delay or prevent the catastrophic release of hazardous materials from a railroad tank car exposed to fires that may result from train derailments. In the FRA�s planned research, test specimens of TPS are to be evaluated in simulated pool fire and torch fire conditions similar to those defined in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. The durations of the fire exposure would extend beyond the 100 minute pool fire and 30 minute torch fire duration specified in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. Pool fire test specimens are applied to a 1 foot by 1 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. Torch fire test specimens are applied to a 4 foot by 4 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. The Volpe Center is looking to perform a minimum of two (2) pool fire tests and two (2) torch fire tests for each TPS. The total number of TPS to be tested has not yet been determined. Although the tests will be similar to those defined in 49 CFR 179 Appendix B, this research may require some modifications to the test protocol including but not limited to additional instrumentation, data collection or varying of test parameters such as duration of the fire exposure. The Volpe Center is also looking for the capability to perform light fabrication of test specimens as detailed above. For examples of possible fabrication requirements, see https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/standards-rulemaking/hazmat/tank-car-thermal-protection-system-list Scope of Information Requested The U.S. DOT Volpe Center is seeking information from commercial testing laboratories, university laboratories, and other interested parties on their willingness, ability, and experience in conducting the simulated pool and torch fire testing planned for various tank car TPS. Descriptions of your facility�s pool and torch fire testing capabilities, including equipment, experience, capacity, resources and staff preparedness for testing tank car TPS. You are encouraged to submit publications of relevant past work. Descriptions of any laboratory accreditation or certification related to pool fire testing. Laboratory hourly rates, technical personnel rates, general facility and equipment usage charges, overhead and other expenses, etc. Descriptions of staff/facility/equipment availability, including any limitations on when fire testing may be conducted (e.g., blackout dates due to seasonal weather conditions) Information on any pre-test data or preliminary sample testing that may be required prior to a full-scale test. Information on your typical post-test laboratory analyses and report formats, and your ability to tailor report/data formats to customer requirements. Description of your facility�s fabrication and assembly capabilities, including: Cutting of 11 gauge steel sheet (0.1196 inches) Cutting of 0.625 inch steel plate Cutting of insulating materials that may generate hazardous airborne particulates such as fiberglass. Mixing and application of coatings to required specifications similar to examples on the PHMSA TPS list. What is the required lead time for fabrication of test specimens? Technical personnel rates, general facility and equipment usage charges, overhead and other expenses, etc. for fabrication of test specimens. Estimated time to conduct one simulated pool fire and one simulated torch fire test including setup, conduct of the test, cooldown, and teardown of test setup. Any other comments that can help the U.S. DOT Volpe Center better define the research scope and direction and ultimately yield technical data beneficial to both the government and industry are welcome. Responses should include the above as well as: Company information Name UEI Address POC information This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and possible issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ). description: The Facilities Construction R&A East CMT of the United States Postal Service is soliciting proposals for a Roof Replacement project, at the United States Postal Service owned Jackson Main Office P&DC, 401 E. South St Jackson, MS 32901-9997 Hinds County. Please see attached Summary of Work. The solicitation will open October 21, 2026 on USPS eSourcing Coupa (see How to Participate below) and close on November 20, 2026. The USPS is concerned with making an award to the supplier striking the appropriate balance of technical features and price. The USPS will not, however, make award to a higher priced offer which provides only marginal additional technical value. As technical scores become closer, then price becomes more important as selection. However, the USPS may not necessarily make an award at the lowest price to achieve a small price savings if better value can be achieved with superior technical features. The successful offeror will be bound by the Contractor's Screening Requirements. Offerors must familiarize themselves with the requirements of Clause F-102. title: J061--Triennial Circuit Breaker and Feeder Testing
description: 1. VAAR 852.219-75 in the solicitation has box (iii), special trade construction contractors (75 percent), marked, while the requirement is coded J061 under NAICS 238210 and FAR 52.219-14 is also included. Please confirm that the 75 percent special trade limitation in box (iii) is the limitation that applies to this award. Confirmed. This requirement is solicited under NAICS 238210. The applicable limitation on subcontracting is VAAR 852.219-75(c)(iii), 75 percent for special trade construction contractors. Offeror must comply with that limitation and submit the signed certificate. 2. The SAM.gov notice shows no set-aside, while the solicitation includes VAAR 852.219-73 (total set-aside for certified SDVOSBs). Please confirm that this requirement is a total SDVOSB set-aside. Confirmed. This is a total SDVOSB set-aside per VAAR 852.219-73 and SF1449 Block 10. NCO 21 will update the SAM.gov notice to reflect the set-aside. Offerors must be certified SDVOSB in SBA Veteran Small Business Certification at time of offer. 3. Section B.1 states that invoices are submitted upon Government inspection and acceptance. Will VA accept two invoices, one after acceptance of field testing and one after acceptance of the coordination study and final report? Yes, the VA will take two invoices. Station/contracting will review these invoices for approval. 4. Amendment 0001 added Attachment C27, Single-Line Schematics. Please confirm whether C27 and the Facility Single Line Diagram together define the full quantities to be tested (MV switches, MV cable runs and vaults, liquid-filled and dry-type transformers, circuit breakers 225A and above, and feeders), or provide an equipment list with counts. Please also identify the buildings covered by "Day 12 + TBD, new facilities since 2017." In the past, a copy of 1-line diagrams was updated with color coding of each test component and a sheet with all quantiles and locations. This should be done to ensure vendor and FMS understands what scope is. 5. For the coordination study and arc flash analysis, is the 2024 study model available to the contractor, and in what software? Is there a required software platform and CAD version for the deliverables? Yes. However, I was just informed that our 2020 circuit breaker testing is the performed format which we can provide. 6. Must the coordination study and arc flash analysis be sealed by a Professional Engineer, and if so, must the engineer be licensed in Nevada? Yes engineering seal is required. No, it does not need to be Nevada. In the past, the previous vendor has had an engineer on staff who did this. 7. Please confirm that the five years of experience in the Contractor Requirements section is verified as a responsibility matter after quotes, and that the quote itself consists of price, the signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, amendment acknowledgments, and the items listed in FAR 52.212-1(a). Confirmed. Contractor Requirements Para 7.3 [5-year experience] will be evaluated as part of responsibility per FAR 9.104 after quotes, not as part of technical acceptability. For quote submission, see FAR 52.212-1(a) as supplemented by Addendum: price on B.2 Schedule, signed SF1449 Block 30 if required, acknowledgment of amendments per B.1 Para 4, signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, and proof of SDVOSB certification status. See also 52.212-3 if not in SAM. 8. Will VA facility electricians perform switching for the outages, and will VA provide temporary power or generator support where emergency branch equipment is de-energized? It is preferred that be in the vendor s scope of work. But verbiage should state that it will be done with Electrical supervisor or designee s authority at time of switching. Vendor should be responsible for the switching of the medium voltage system (25KV). This would be the P/Q switch in Boiler plant yard, medium voltage switches, and transformers in/on the facility down stream from the P/Q switch. VA electricians may assist with switching for 600 volts and less to aid in the testing. This must be arranged in the presented schedule to ensure proper VA staff is available. 9. What is the anticipated award date and the targeted notice-to-proceed window, so offerors can hold test crews for the night schedule? Anticipated award is within 2-3 weeks after the 11/9/2026 due date, subject to evaluations. NTP is intended ASAP after award per SOW 8.1. Offerors should plan to start coordination within 1 week of NTP. We will not require crews to be held prior to NTP. 10. Will a site visit be offered before the quote due date, and if so, will attendance be optional? VA high encourages site visits to visit equipment types, locations, and quantities. This has not been a bidding mandate to attend, but is encouraged. 11. Is there a deadline for questions, and will answers be issued by amendment? Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers that affect the SOW or terms will be issued by formal amendment to all offerors. Administrative clarifications may be answered by email. 12. The quote submission method and address, and the question deadline. Quotes shall be submitted by email to alex.arter@va.gov. Quotes are due November 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific Time. File size: split emails if over 20MB. Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers affecting SOW/terms/pricing will be issued by formal amendment. 13. Whether a site visit at the Ioannis A. Lougaris VAMC (Reno) will be held, and its date. A site visit is planned. Attendance will be optional. Date/time and meeting location will be issued by amendment once coordinated with Engineering. Offerors are encouraged to attend to verify existing conditions. No energized work will be performed during the site visit. 14. Breaker and feeder quantities by voltage class (LV/MV), and whether protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in scope. From the previous tests. There are: 11 MV Switches 10 MV Transformers 477 Circuit Breakers 570 Feeder Cables 27 LV Transformers Protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in the scope. The arc-flash label updates are to have their associated room numbers on them and must be done with professional engravings (i.e. no hand drawn labels). 15. Planned outage windows, and whether shutdowns must be after hours or on weekends. Yes. Per SOW 8.6, Electrical Testing shall be performed during Off Hours - 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM, weekends, and federal holidays. Photography work shall be performed during Normal Hours (Mon-Fri 6AM-6PM). The sequencing in SOW 8.1 shall be used as the basis for pricing. Final outage windows will be coordinated with the COR 2 weeks in advance per SOW 8.7 to minimize impact to patient care. 16. Required standard and deliverables (for example, NETA MTS and VHA Directive 1028 reporting). The required standard and deliverables are to be adhered to the most concurrent American National Standard: Standard for Maintenance Testing Specification for Electrical Power Equipment and Systems (ANSI/NETA MTS) as well as the VHA Directive 1028. This can be found in section 7.1 and 7.14 in the SOW. Additional code requirements can also be found in this section.

title: Supply Thermal Protection Systems for Railroad Tank Cars
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. Purpose This RFI seeks information regarding providing Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) for railroad tank cars to the U.S. DOT Volpe Center. A qualified vendor must demonstrate they are able to provide either complete test specimens as detailed further below or sufficient materials to fabricate completed test specimens without the need for specialized facilities or techniques. Qualified vendors are requested to respond as detailed further below, which includes capability, small business classification, estimated lead time including any risks that may impact delivery, and any other industry concerns the government might consider before solicitation. The intent is to gather information to inform a possible future procurement or contract. Background The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) is conducting research into the performance of TPS for railroad tank cars. TPS are designed to delay or prevent the catastrophic release of hazardous materials from a railroad tank car exposed to fires that may result from train derailments. In the FRA�s planned research, test specimens of TPS are to be evaluated in simulated pool fire and torch fire conditions similar to those defined in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. The durations of the fire exposure would extend beyond the 100 minute pool fire and 30 minute torch fire duration specified in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. Pool fire test specimens are applied to a 1 foot by 1 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. Torch fire test specimens are applied to a 4 foot by 4 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. The Volpe Center is looking to procure a minimum of two (2) pool fire test specimens and two (2) torch fire test specimens for each TPS. Multiple TPS of different construction from the same vendor may be considered. The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) maintains a list of tank car TPS that have been tested and shown to comply with the requirements of Appendix B to 49 CFR Part 179. Inclusion on this list is not a requirement for a TPS to be used on a tank car. There is a preference of TPS that are currently on the PHMSA list and/or being used on tank cars, but other systems may be considered. Scope of Information Requested The U.S. DOT Volpe Center is seeking information from tank car thermal protection system manufacturers and/or vendors, on their willingness, ability, and requirements to provide the physical specimens as well as material and installation information needed to conduct the above fire testing research. Description of how the TPS is assembled. Example : 1 inch insulation � Brand XXX 1 inch fiberglass � generic 11 gauge steel jacket � generic 10 mils coating � Brand YYY, Component A and Component B in 1:1 volume ratio Include any relevant brand names or item numbers specific to this system. Also include any required surface preparation or other processing steps. Is the TPS currently used on railroad tank cars? If so, is it on the PHMSA approved list here: https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/standards-rulemaking/hazmat/tank-car-thermal-protection-system-list Are you capable of supplying fully assembled test specimens? If YES, do you require government furnished plates on which to apply the TPS? If NO, are you prepared to supply detailed instructions on fabrication, including any considerations for required equipment, cutting, bonding, forming, attachment, surface preparation, mixing, curing/drying or any other fabrication steps? What is the required lead time for either assembled test specimens or sufficient materials for third-party fabrication? Your willingness to sell TPS for this third-party testing effort. Availability and willingness to share any existing pool and/or torch fire testing data on the subject TPS, and any sensitivities or proprietary data protections that would be needed prior to sharing such information. Estimated prices of either assembled test specimens or sufficient materials for third party fabrication. Any other comments that can help the U.S. DOT Volpe Center better define the research scope and direction and ultimately yield technical data beneficial to both the government and industry are welcome. Responses should include the above as well as: Company information Name UEI Address POC information This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and possible issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation for bids, quotations, and proposals, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a competitive contract. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government.
