title: Smartphone Style Mobile Barcode Scanners
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) to obtain capability statements and potential feedback for an upcoming Library of Congress (LOC) requirement. Specifically, the Library of Congress (Library) requires support to procure twenty-five (25) rugged, smartphone-style enterprise mobile computers built with an integrated barcode scanner for fast data collection in library environments. The smartphone-style enterprise mobile computers shall have an Android OS, be lightweight, contain touchscreen capabilities, USB charging, contain a replaceable battery, and have an optional trigger accessory available. The smartphone-style enterprise mobile computers shall support support the Finding EnvironmenT for Collected Holdings (FETCH) software to maintain the Library�s inventory at the offsite facilities, include an ongoing annual maintenance plan, software updates, hardware repair and replacement for each device. In order to obtain this information, the Library is seeking capabilities statements, rough orders of magnitude estimates, input on the Statement of Work, or any other information your business would care to provide in order to help the Library understand the possible solutions available on the commercial marketplace. All information received shall be reviewed to help the Library inform its possible future acquisition decisions relating to this requirement. Participation in this RFI is voluntary only and is no guarantee of future business. As an RFI, this is NOT an official solicitation. The Library is not seeking to obtain official proposals at this time as a result of this notice. The Library is seeking outside information from potential offerors as a way to perform supplemental market research. No contract shall be awarded as a result of this RFI. This notice solely constitutes market research. Under NO circumstances shall any expenses be repaid as a result of contractor engagement with RFI this notice. Offerors are encouraged to ask questions or provide feedback so that the LOC may enhance its understanding to reflect a more accurate business environment. Attached is a draft Statement of Work. Offerors are encouraged to provide feedback on this document as well, and all comments/questions/suggestions shall be considered (this is not a guarantee that they will be answered or reflected in the final solicitation). Finally, rough orders of magnitude in terms of pricing is also being asked for. Please note, these would be estimates only and serve only the purposes of market research. These are NOT official quotes, but are considered to be high level rough ballpark estimates of other marketplace solutions.

title: Robins RAPID Construction OTA Progressive Design Build Fiber Replacement
description: FA8501-27-RAPID-CIRCUIT F1-170129-OTA Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: RAPID Progressive Design-Build to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation UHHZ170129 Description The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation at Robins AFB, GA. The requirement includes replacement of all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout circuit F-01. This will include replacement and removal all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes. This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Purpose The purpose of this Area of Interest is to obtain commercially viable, safe, and schedule-credible solutions to design plans for and to perform the replacement of expired high-risk Circuit F01 cabling in order to prevent operational risk, mission delays, and compounding economic costs due to infrastructure failure at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The Government requires an integrated approach to address the design, removal of deteriorated cables and replacement with new cable in The Fowler Substation. The selected approach must provide a practical path to execute the work while minimizing disruption to aircraft operations and controlling construction, safety, environmental, and schedule risks. Project Background and Existing Conditions Circuit F-01 has surpassed its operational lifecycle, creating a high-probability risk for catastrophic failure. If the remaining aged portion is not replaced, the installation faces risk of emergency repair premiums and disruption to sustaining airfield infrastructure, supporting safe aircraft movement, installation readiness, and continued mission operations. The work area is slightly congested and impacted by various airfield operations. The Fowler Substation Circuit F-01 will remain in full operation during the entire duration of the project by back feeding with circuit ties. Project Areas Phase 1 (Preconstruction & Collaborative Design): Collaborative design development stakeholders to achieve 65%, site surveys, risk mitigation planning, schedule and establishment of an open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) IAW with all other aspects of the SOO. Phase 2 (Final Design & Construction Execution) Completion of final design and full construction execution (exercised upon agreement). Safely construct the facility/project within the agreed GMP and schedule. Assume hazardous materials exist. Address requirements for worker notification, abatement, and disposal. Employ a safety and health professional to provide a HASP per DoDI 6055.01. Comply with Robins Environmental Requirements (Section 01560) submitting Waste Management Report/Landfill Waste Tickets, Solid Waste Disposal Plan, and Qualified Recycling Program (QRP). Appropriately coordinate Stormwater & Erosion Control. Structure execution to allow for payable milestones payments, as well as all other aspects outlined in the SOO. Project-Specific Objectives and Phasing Replace all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout the distribution of circuit F-01 in its entirety of multiple different installation facilities, while remaining in full operation besides outages and removing and replacing all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes. Address specific phasing to accommodate congested areas. OTA & RAPID Framework Approach This project is being executed as an Area of Interest (AOI) under the overarching RAPID (Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development) Umbrella Program Notice. In accordance with the RAPID framework, this project utilizes a Progressive Design-Build approach under the standalone statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government will be expecting a 100% completed design package and/or specific phasing and repair requirements followed by the completion of the construction or performance of the designed actions. Competitive Selection Process Phase 1 Solution Brief Requirements The Government reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to determine that a response which does not conform to the requirements or instructions contained in this announcement is ineligible for further consideration. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in a clear, concise, and organized manner in accordance with this announcement. To facilitate an efficient review, responses shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions and formatting requirements contained in this announcement. Failure to comply with these requirements may increase the risk that the response will not be considered for further evaluation. The Government will evaluate them to identify the most highly qualified parties. Submission Requirement should be submitted by 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on or before 20 November 2026. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief consisting of no more than five written pages (5), excluding the cover page. Email is the official form of submission for responses. Surety letters may be attached without counting towards 5 page limit. Page format should be 8.5 x 11. The Solution Brief shall include: Cover Page Company name UEI Mailing address Primary point of contact Email address and telephone number Identification of this RAPID AOI Executive Summary, Team Composition, and Organization Summary of the respondent�s qualifications and anticipated delivery capability Explanation of why the team is qualified for the anticipated requirement The team�s understanding of the Robins Air Force Base operational environment The team�s experience working in occupied facilities, congested site logistics, complex mechanical/electrical system integrations, and adherence to stringent environmental and safety standards. (e.g., hazardous material abatement, and experience with Department of War/Air Force Standards). The team�s proposed approach to Phase 1 collaboration and risk reduction Identification of any material capability, staffing, access, bonding, or teaming assumptions. Past Relevant Construction Capability and Experience Minimum Requirement: The Company must demonstrate a minimum of five (5) years of experience successfully executing construction projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity. Focus: Historical performance in occupied facilities, managing congested site logistics, complex mechanical/electrical system integrations, adhering to environmental and safety standards.(e.g., hazardous material abatement, and experience with Department of Defense/Air Force Standards). Note that while DoD experience is considered, it will not be a deciding factor in determining a firm more qualified. Financial Capacity and Bonding A statement of financial capacity to perform the anticipated work Current single-project and aggregate bonding capacity, if bonds are anticipated; Name of surety Any other information necessary to demonstrate capacity to perform the anticipated project. Construction Execution and Phasing Approach Methodology for physical work execution Utility outage coordination Evaluation & Selection Criteria The Government will utilize a two-step, Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process mapped to the RAPID framework to select the Design-Builder. In accordance with PDB methodology, price will not be evaluated during the initial selection process. Selection is based on qualifications, experience, and collaborative capabilities. Step 1: RAPID Phase 1 Equivalent Evaluation

Note: Successful offeror will be required to submit a Sub-Contracting Plan and Project Specific Safety Plan acceptable to the USPS Contracting Officer before a Notice to Proceed (NTP) is issued. The successful offeror will be bound by the Contractor's Screening Requirements. Offerors must familiarize themselves with the requirements of Clause F-102. title: Mather Fueling System Repairs
description: Project is located in Mather, CA. Includes all work to install a sampling gauge hatch on a manway, install a clock type mechanical gauge on a manway, recoat the exterior of the tank, replace the collision barriers, add a catwalk that extends across the entirety of the tank, and replace the audible and visual alarms. o Fix the remote containment basin drainage issue. o Replace the asphalt on the NE side of the fueling facility. o Repair the refueler parking concrete. o Replace the dispenser fuel monitor with a non-coalescing filter and install a water draw off system with a hand pump. o Replace the asphalt near the loading/unloading facility with a concrete path. o Replace POL building of the same size and at the same location. o Complete supplying, installation, and testing ATG system on Fuel Storage Tank, AVGAS. o Relocate the generator that is inside the compartmentalized area.

description: VA Northern California Health Care System 612A4-27-018 Page 4 of 5 Statement of Work Replace B650 3rd and 2nd Flooring Project #612A4-27-018 General Intention: The purpose of this project is to replace flooring, resilient base, stainless steel corner guards, and paint throughout B650 3rd and 2nd Floor of the Sacramento Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) of VA Northern California Healthcare System (VANCHCS). Contractor shall furnish all labor and materials needed to perform all demolition, replacement, and installation required by this scope as required by specifications. Visits to the site by bidders may be made only by appointment with the Contracting Officer (CO) for the project. A preliminary/pre-proposal site visit is strongly encouraged and shall be coordinated with the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). Location of work; the geographic location for service(s) are the following areas: Sacramento VA Medical Center 10535 Hospital Way Mather, CA 95655 Buildings: 650 3rd and 2nd Floors The contractor shall consider that there are no staging areas available within the facility premises. If necessary, staging areas may be put into effect at the discretion of the COR, depending on availability. The Contractor shall note that there is absolutely NO Contractor employee parking in Patient Parking designated areas. VANCHCS will not invalidate or make reimbursement for parking violations for the Contractor under any conditions. The contractor will be responsible for disposing of all equipment components and trash demolished or replaced as part of this project. The contractor is responsible for following infection control procedures per VA specifications and site infection control protocols. Any work activities that generate noise or disruption sufficient to impact patient care, disturb patients, or interfere with staff operations must be conducted only after normal working hours or on weekends. The proposed product shall be similar in appearance and shall match the color, texture, pattern, and finish of the specified product to the satisfaction of VA Engineering. The Contractor shall submit product data, samples, color charts, and other information necessary for VA Engineering s evaluation and approval. The contractor shall remove and install new accessories associated with the flooring. Carpet and luxury vinyl tiles to include, but not limited to, subfloors, carpet tack strips, carpet padding, and vinyl glue. The contractor shall paint all rooms located on the 2nd and 3rd floors of Building 650 per specification Section 09 06 00, Schedule of Finishes. The contractor is responsible for providing all necessary materials, labor, and equipment to complete both the repair and painting work. The VA will provide a paint plan as the installation date approaches. For installation purposes and material lengths, the contractor shall follow wall mockup located outside the Engineering Suite at Building 650. Contractor to coordinate visit with COR. title: J061--Triennial Circuit Breaker and Feeder Testing
description: 1. VAAR 852.219-75 in the solicitation has box (iii), special trade construction contractors (75 percent), marked, while the requirement is coded J061 under NAICS 238210 and FAR 52.219-14 is also included. Please confirm that the 75 percent special trade limitation in box (iii) is the limitation that applies to this award. Confirmed. This requirement is solicited under NAICS 238210. The applicable limitation on subcontracting is VAAR 852.219-75(c)(iii), 75 percent for special trade construction contractors. Offeror must comply with that limitation and submit the signed certificate. 2. The SAM.gov notice shows no set-aside, while the solicitation includes VAAR 852.219-73 (total set-aside for certified SDVOSBs). Please confirm that this requirement is a total SDVOSB set-aside. Confirmed. This is a total SDVOSB set-aside per VAAR 852.219-73 and SF1449 Block 10. NCO 21 will update the SAM.gov notice to reflect the set-aside. Offerors must be certified SDVOSB in SBA Veteran Small Business Certification at time of offer. 3. Section B.1 states that invoices are submitted upon Government inspection and acceptance. Will VA accept two invoices, one after acceptance of field testing and one after acceptance of the coordination study and final report? Yes, the VA will take two invoices. Station/contracting will review these invoices for approval. 4. Amendment 0001 added Attachment C27, Single-Line Schematics. Please confirm whether C27 and the Facility Single Line Diagram together define the full quantities to be tested (MV switches, MV cable runs and vaults, liquid-filled and dry-type transformers, circuit breakers 225A and above, and feeders), or provide an equipment list with counts. Please also identify the buildings covered by "Day 12 + TBD, new facilities since 2017." In the past, a copy of 1-line diagrams was updated with color coding of each test component and a sheet with all quantiles and locations. This should be done to ensure vendor and FMS understands what scope is. 5. For the coordination study and arc flash analysis, is the 2024 study model available to the contractor, and in what software? Is there a required software platform and CAD version for the deliverables? Yes. However, I was just informed that our 2020 circuit breaker testing is the performed format which we can provide. 6. Must the coordination study and arc flash analysis be sealed by a Professional Engineer, and if so, must the engineer be licensed in Nevada? Yes engineering seal is required. No, it does not need to be Nevada. In the past, the previous vendor has had an engineer on staff who did this. 7. Please confirm that the five years of experience in the Contractor Requirements section is verified as a responsibility matter after quotes, and that the quote itself consists of price, the signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, amendment acknowledgments, and the items listed in FAR 52.212-1(a). Confirmed. Contractor Requirements Para 7.3 [5-year experience] will be evaluated as part of responsibility per FAR 9.104 after quotes, not as part of technical acceptability. For quote submission, see FAR 52.212-1(a) as supplemented by Addendum: price on B.2 Schedule, signed SF1449 Block 30 if required, acknowledgment of amendments per B.1 Para 4, signed VAAR 852.219-75 certificate, and proof of SDVOSB certification status. See also 52.212-3 if not in SAM. 8. Will VA facility electricians perform switching for the outages, and will VA provide temporary power or generator support where emergency branch equipment is de-energized? It is preferred that be in the vendor s scope of work. But verbiage should state that it will be done with Electrical supervisor or designee s authority at time of switching. Vendor should be responsible for the switching of the medium voltage system (25KV). This would be the P/Q switch in Boiler plant yard, medium voltage switches, and transformers in/on the facility down stream from the P/Q switch. VA electricians may assist with switching for 600 volts and less to aid in the testing. This must be arranged in the presented schedule to ensure proper VA staff is available. 9. What is the anticipated award date and the targeted notice-to-proceed window, so offerors can hold test crews for the night schedule? Anticipated award is within 2-3 weeks after the 11/9/2026 due date, subject to evaluations. NTP is intended ASAP after award per SOW 8.1. Offerors should plan to start coordination within 1 week of NTP. We will not require crews to be held prior to NTP. 10. Will a site visit be offered before the quote due date, and if so, will attendance be optional? VA high encourages site visits to visit equipment types, locations, and quantities. This has not been a bidding mandate to attend, but is encouraged. 11. Is there a deadline for questions, and will answers be issued by amendment? Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers that affect the SOW or terms will be issued by formal amendment to all offerors. Administrative clarifications may be answered by email. 12. The quote submission method and address, and the question deadline. Quotes shall be submitted by email to alex.arter@va.gov. Quotes are due November 9, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific Time. File size: split emails if over 20MB. Submit questions NLT 11/02/2026 12PM PST to alex.arter@va.gov. Answers affecting SOW/terms/pricing will be issued by formal amendment. 13. Whether a site visit at the Ioannis A. Lougaris VAMC (Reno) will be held, and its date. A site visit is planned. Attendance will be optional. Date/time and meeting location will be issued by amendment once coordinated with Engineering. Offerors are encouraged to attend to verify existing conditions. No energized work will be performed during the site visit. 14. Breaker and feeder quantities by voltage class (LV/MV), and whether protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in scope. From the previous tests. There are: 11 MV Switches 10 MV Transformers 477 Circuit Breakers 570 Feeder Cables 27 LV Transformers Protective relay testing and arc-flash label updates are in the scope. The arc-flash label updates are to have their associated room numbers on them and must be done with professional engravings (i.e. no hand drawn labels). 15. Planned outage windows, and whether shutdowns must be after hours or on weekends. Yes. Per SOW 8.6, Electrical Testing shall be performed during Off Hours - 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM, weekends, and federal holidays. Photography work shall be performed during Normal Hours (Mon-Fri 6AM-6PM). The sequencing in SOW 8.1 shall be used as the basis for pricing. Final outage windows will be coordinated with the COR 2 weeks in advance per SOW 8.7 to minimize impact to patient care. 16. Required standard and deliverables (for example, NETA MTS and VHA Directive 1028 reporting). The required standard and deliverables are to be adhered to the most concurrent American National Standard: Standard for Maintenance Testing Specification for Electrical Power Equipment and Systems (ANSI/NETA MTS) as well as the VHA Directive 1028. This can be found in section 7.1 and 7.14 in the SOW. Additional code requirements can also be found in this section.

title: Pensacola Harbor Navigation Channel Maintenance Dredging
description: This requirement is for hydraulic cutterhead pipeline dredges, trailing suction hopper dredges, and/or mechanical dredges with scows. Dredges must be capable of dredging to a depth of 30 feet and be complete with crew, management staff and support equipment including tugs and various other floating plants as would normally be expected to support a large dredging operation. The material type expected for this requirement will be maintenance material typical for Pensacola Entrance Channel composed of sand. Material dredged will be placed west of the Pensacola Entrance Channel along Perdido Key Beach.

Planned outage windows, and whether shutdowns must be after hours or on weekends. Yes. Per SOW 8.6, Electrical Testing shall be performed during Off Hours - 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM, weekends, and federal holidays. Photography work shall be performed during Normal Hours (Mon-Fri 6AM-6PM). The sequencing in SOW 8.1 shall be used as the basis for pricing. Final outage windows will be coordinated with the COR 2 weeks in advance per SOW 8.7 to minimize impact to patient care. 16. Required standard and deliverables (for example, NETA MTS and VHA Directive 1028 reporting). The required standard and deliverables are to be adhered to the most concurrent American National Standard: Standard for Maintenance Testing Specification for Electrical Power Equipment and Systems (ANSI/NETA MTS) as well as the VHA Directive 1028. This can be found in section 7.1 and 7.14 in the SOW. Additional code requirements can also be found in this section.

title: Medtronic cardiovascular "procedural packages"
description: This is a sources sought notice. The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support is seeking sources capable of providing Medtronic cardiovascular "procedural packages". The "procedural package" includes the cardiovascular products and ancillary accessories (such as needles for entry and guidewire) that are necessary for the physician to perform the cardiovascular surgeries. The product mix that makes up the "procedural package" varies based on the individual needs of the patient. All products must be approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The products that make up the �procedural package� must be delivered Just-In-Time (JIT), Direct Vendor Delivery (DVD) and Consignment. Under the JIT delivery method, the Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) calls the manufacturer�s field representative who carries the products into the MTF just-in-time for the surgery. The manufacturer�s sales representative may bring many sizes and types of implants and other auxiliary products to the surgery along with the instrumentation sets. Under the DVD method an order for products is placed through ECAT and the products are delivered direct to the customer via any transportation carrier. Under the consignment method, a Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) will have the products that make up the procedural package consigned to their facility. At the request of the MTF�s, the manufacturer is required to have a qualified representative on site at the MTF�s within the timeframe specified by the facility necessary to meet their requirements. The manufacturer�s representative provides technical advice and guidance to the physicians before, during and after implantation. Furthermore, technical support is available twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week. This is a Request For Information (RFI) and does not commit the U.S. Government to issue a solicitation, make an award or pay any costs associated with responding to this announcement. All submitted information shall remain with the U.S. Government and will not be returned. Your response to this RFI shall be submitted electronically in PDF format and emailed to kathleen.adamow-wandall@dla.mil

Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE

title: Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. Delivery Schedule-The offeror's ability to meet or improve upon the Government's required delivery schedule, including proposed lead times for equipment delivery and startup services. Price-The total evaluated price for all CLINs. Past Performance- The Government may consider an offeror's past performance in supplying and delivering products similar in scope and complexity to the requirements of this solicitation. Evaluation may include the offeror's history of meeting delivery commitments, providing complete and accurate shipments, responding to customer concerns, and overall performance associated with the delivery of comparable equipment. Technical Compliance, Delivery Schedule, and Price, Past Performance will be considered in determining the quotation that represents the Best Value to the Government. The Government may award to other than the lowest-priced offeror if the additional value associated with a higher-rated quotation warrants the additional cost. Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered at https://www.sam.gov/. title: Z1DA--642-22-104 | Upgrade Substation Building 2 Phase 1 for Philadelphia VAMC
description: 642-22-104, 36C24426R0088, Upgrade Substation Building 2, Phase 1, PHL CMCVAMC Proposal Due Date: 11/20/2026 at 4:00pm EST. Email proposals to Kevin Rodgers at kevin.rodgers2@va.gov. Corporal Michael J. Crescenz Medical Center (CMC VAMC) requires replacement of Electrical Substations 1 and 2 in order to increase electrical capacity to support future facility projects. The existing substations are approximately 29 years old and require replacement to support current and future electrical demands. This project will replace Electrical Substations 1 and 2 with new 480/277V substations each containing a 1500 kVA transformer. A temporary 480/277V substation with a 1500 kVA transformer shall be installed to maintain electrical service to the facility during demolition and construction activities. Upon completion of construction, the temporary substation shall remain installed as a spare substation for the facility. All work shall be phased to minimize service outages and maintain continuous operation of the medical center. Defined and issued bid documents (drawings and specifications) will serve as the basis of this construction project.

title: Q525--LASER SERVICES - BUFFALO UROLOGY Holmium (30 and 80 Watt) Lasers CO2 Laser Lithotripsy (ESWL) Laser
description: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. This is a Request for Information (RFI)/ Sources Sought Notice only and is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10 Market Research, in order to conduct market research. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or a guarantee to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation, if issued. This announcement is based on the best information available at this time and is subject to future modification. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 621999 All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services, Small Business Size Standard $20.5 Million. Purpose and Objectives: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, and the Buffalo VA Medical Center anticipate a 5 year contract for Holmium (30 and 80 watts), CO2, and Lithotripsy (ESWL) Laser Services to include the unit, technician and all supplies. The surgical suites at the Buffalo VAMC are specifically wired to handle an electrical current that is 30amps and 240 volts or less. It is required that all equipment utilized in each suite, plug directly into the electrical wall outlet without the use of an adapter or transformer. The Contractor shall make the units and New York State certified technician available to the Buffalo VAMC in accordance with a schedule mutually agreed upon by both the VA Medical Center and Contractor. Contractor shall conduct performance within the manufacturer s specifications. Contractor shall provide all equipment, supplies and New York State certified technician. Duties and Response times include, but are not limited to: Contractor will be liable for damages should patient injury result due to laser malfunction. The Contractor shall make available all the following lasers, supplies, labor and certified technician available to the Buffalo VAMC in accordance with a schedule mutually agreed upon by both the VA Medical Center and Contractor. Holmium 30 Watt & 80 Watt Lasers CO2 Laser Lithotripsy Laser Contractor shall conduct performance tests of the units to ensure that the units are in the highest level working condition in accordance with the manufacturer s specifications. Contractor shall maintain all laser equipment in safe and operating condition at all times. The contractor is responsible to ensure that all corrective, preventative and all components of the system will operate at optimum performance to provide the best possible treatment to the patients and minimize downtime. Up to date preventative maintenance and corrective maintenance records for the equipment must be made available to the Buffalo VAMC Biomedical Engineering Department by the Contractor upon request. Contractor shall bill in accordance with the services in the PWS and coordinating pricing in the Schedule of Supplies and Services. Contractor shall only bill for actual supplies used in each case. Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, supervision, equipment, and services as required in this PWS. The Contractor shall be responsible for completing all reporting requirements established by the contract. Contractor shall be responsible for assuring the accuracy and completeness of all laser use records and other documents as well as the timely submission of each. Laser Use Records shall be completed by the Contractor for each case which utilizes a Laser. Contractor shall comply with the contract requirements regarding the appropriate instructions, timetables, and technical assistance as required. Contractor shall ensure that all technicians while on VA property wear a company identification badge. Contractor shall ensure all Contract Technicians familiar and are required to follow all VA policies and procedures. Contractor shall provide all equipment, supplies and New York State certified technician. Place of Performance: Department of Veterans Affairs Buffalo VA Medical Center, 3495 Bailey Ave, Buffalo NY 14215 Response: Please submit your response via email in accordance with the following instructions: Responses shall be no more than 12 pages in length Emails are limited to 10mb per each. Cover page with responses to the Specific Response Items listed in the section below. Detail your firm s ability, capability, and responsibility to deliver the above referenced services for the period of time identified. Detail the each unit, and what supplies/disposables would be required to operate the unit per procedure. (e.g., Fibers, needles, etc.) Include a statement of Contractor s experience providing Holmium (30 and 80 watts), CO2, and Lithotripsy (ESWL) Laser Services to the Department of Veterans Affairs or other entity, to include: VA Location/Name of Company Contract Length Estimated contract Value Number of Hours/Weeks Submit your response via email, with the RFI number in the subject line to: Kiandra Venson at Kiandra.Venson@va.gov Submit your response by 4:00 PM Eastern Time on November 20, 2026. title: USSS Construction Management & Engineering Services
description: Request for Information Construction Management Services NAICS Code 541330, Engineering Services Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) Agency: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Secret Service (USSS) Response Due Date: November 20, 2026 Point of Contact: Kimberly Johnson, Contracting Officer, Assistant Division Chief, Office of Procurement 1. Purpose The U.S. Secret Service is conducting market research to identify qualified construction management firms capable of supporting future construction, renovation, design-management, and related task-order requirements. This Request for Information is issued solely for planning and market research purposes. USSS is seeking information from firms operating under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541330, Engineering Services, including small businesses and socioeconomic small-business concerns, that possess the organizational capacity, technical expertise, security capability, and geographic reach necessary to support future construction activities. Responses to this RFI will assist USSS in assessing industry capability, the availability of qualified firms, small-business participation, competition, bonding capacity, staffing resources, geographic coverage, and potential acquisition approaches for a future BPA or IDIQ type contract with the USSS. This RFI is not a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment, or promise by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2. Anticipated Requirement Description The U.S. Secret Service (USSS) anticipates a nationwide requirement for construction management and related design, engineering, security, infrastructure, and maintenance services at Government-owned or leased facilities and other Government-designated locations throughout the United States and its territories. Work may include new construction, renovations, retrofits, system upgrades, emergency repairs, and sustainment activities performed in occupied, operational, secure, or time-sensitive environments. Depending on the task order, firms may be required to provide services across the full project lifecycle, including: Planning, requirements development, site surveys, existing-condition assessments, project scoping, and cost estimating. Architectural and engineering design management, design review, value engineering, constructability review, and preparation of procurement-ready design documents. Acquisition and preconstruction support, including bid evaluation and contractor-vetting assistance. Construction administration and management, including quality control, safety and schedule oversight, stakeholder coordination, phased work, and management of design changes. Equipment procurement, fabrication, installation, systems integration, testing, commissioning, documentation, training, maintenance, repair, and urgent-response support, as specified in individual task orders. Anticipated task orders may cover one or more of the following service areas: Physical security enhancements: Perimeter controls, security booths and command posts, vehicle and pedestrian access points, site improvements, structural hardening, ballistic or blast-resistant features, secure rooms, doors, gates, locks, and related protective measures. Electronic security systems: Video surveillance and management, intrusion detection, access control, command-and-control, intercom and notification systems, supporting networks and equipment, system programming, cybersecurity hardening, integration, testing, and operator training. Infrastructure and building systems: Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, communications, emergency power, structured and fiber-optic cabling, fire and life-safety systems, HVAC, environmental controls, and building-management or monitoring platforms needed to support security and mission continuity. Preventive and corrective maintenance: Inspection, testing, calibration, software and firmware maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, component replacement, emergency response, spare-parts support, lifecycle assessment, and documentation for covered systems and infrastructure. The scope is broad and non-exhaustive. Each task order may establish the applicable locations, technical requirements, deliverables, performance standards, schedule, security restrictions, acceptance criteria, and maintenance obligations. Firms may need to integrate new, existing, legacy, or proprietary systems while minimizing disruption and maintaining safety, security, and continuity of operations. The Government anticipates that some future requirements may involve concurrent task orders of significant value. Respondents should identify their capacity to manage multiple projects simultaneously, including their ability to provide appropriately cleared personnel when required. 3. Industry Information Requested Interested firms are requested to complete and submit the attached Interested Vendor Questionnaire, U.S. Secret Service Construction Management Services, Request for Information, along with the supporting information identified below. 4. Submission Requirements Interested firms should submit the following: A completed Interested Vendor Questionnaire. A capability statement of no more than three pages. Information for up to three relevant completed projects from the past three years. Supporting project documentation, as available. Evidence of SAM.gov registration and applicable socioeconomic certifications, if requested or applicable. Responses should be submitted electronically in searchable PDF format to Kimberly Johnson, email: kimberly.m.johnson@usss.dhs.gov no later than November 20, 2026, 4:00 pm Eastern Standard time. The email subject line should read: RFI Response: USSS Construction Management Services � [Company Name] 5. Additional Information Respondents are encouraged to identify any recommended acquisition, contract-structure, ordering, scope-management, or small-business participation considerations that may help USSS develop a future requirement. Responses should not include sensitive operational, security, proprietary, or controlled information unless specifically authorized by applicable submission instructions. Firms should clearly mark proprietary information submitted in response to this RFI. The Government may use information received in response to this RFI to refine its acquisition strategy, determine the appropriate small-business approach, establish anticipated contract requirements, and develop any future solicitation. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation or award a contract because of this RFI. 6. RFI Disclaimer This RFI is for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment by the Government. Submission of a response is voluntary and will not result in reimbursement of any costs incurred. A response to this RFI is not required to participate in any future solicitation, should one be issued. Attachment: Interested Vendor Questionnaire, U.S. Secret Service Construction Management Services Request for Information

description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. Failure Escalation & Root Cause Analysis: Describe your engineering experience and/or procedures for performing root cause failure investigations and delivering Failed Item Analysis Reports (FIARs) and

title: CFLHD Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for Architect-Engineer Design Services
description: Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services The Federal Highway Administration, Central Federal Lands Highway Division (CFLHD), anticipates soliciting and awarding multiple Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for A-E services with a partial small business set-aside. CFLHD provides engineering and construction services on projects in the states of Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming on behalf of Federal Land Management Agencies and other Agencies. These Agencies include: the National Park Service (NPS); USDA Forest Service (Forest Service); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS); Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) and Tribal Governments; Bureau of Land Management (BLM); Department of Defense (DOD); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE); and the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR). The shared capacity of the IDIQs will be $60 million. The acquisition will be solicited and awarded on a competitive basis and is being made under the North America Industry Classification Code 541330 and is open to all business concerns. The planned duration for the contracts is a total of five years. Projects are typically located in environmentally sensitive areas that necessitate context-sensitive design techniques and processes. Project topography type and climatic zones vary greatly including coastal, mountainous, desert and plains regions. Projects will primarily involve improvements to low-volume and low-speed roadways ranging from 3R (resurfacing, restoration and rehabilitation) to full reconstruction. The geographic jurisdiction of CFLHD includes, but is not limited to, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming.

The planned duration for the contracts is a total of five years. Projects are typically located in environmentally sensitive areas that necessitate context-sensitive design techniques and processes. Project topography type and climatic zones vary greatly including coastal, mountainous, desert and plains regions. Projects will primarily involve improvements to low-volume and low-speed roadways ranging from 3R (resurfacing, restoration and rehabilitation) to full reconstruction. The geographic jurisdiction of CFLHD includes, but is not limited to, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming.
